items.title: National Commission on Dam Safety Holds 12th Meeting
items.whyInNews: The 12th meeting of the National Commission on Dam Safety (NCDS) was held in New Delhi on July 17, 2026, to discuss dam safety issues.
items.summary: The National Commission on Dam Safety (NCDS) held its 12th meeting in New Delhi, chaired by Dr. Bharat Jhunjhunwala. The meeting discussed various dam safety issues, including the implementation of the Dam Safety Act, 2021. The Commission also reviewed the progress made by states in implementing dam safety measures. The meeting was attended by representatives from various state governments and central agencies.

items.title: India Raises Issues of Students, Travellers with US
items.whyInNews: India raised issues of students and travellers with the US, regarding the new visa rule, on July 16, 2026.

items.title: India's gig internet workforce may reach 17-21 million by 2030
items.whyInNews: A report by Bengaluru firm Redseer states that India's gig internet workforce is expected to grow to 17-21 million by 2030. The report highlights the growth of the gig economy in India, with full-time gig workers earning up to 2.5 times the monthly net income of workers in comparable formal and informal occupations.
items.summary: The report by Redseer highlights the growth of the gig economy in India, with a projected workforce of 17-21 million by 2030. This growth is driven by the increasing demand for delivery, ride-hailing, and home services. The gig economy is expected to provide better earning opportunities for workers, with full-time gig workers earning up to 2.5 times the monthly net income of workers in comparable formal and informal occupations. The report also notes that the gig economy will continue to play a significant role in India's economic growth.

items.title: Centre concedes to States' demands on Higher Education Bill
items.whyInNews: The Centre has agreed to amend at least two clauses of the Higher Education Bill, leaving State universities out of certain aspects of the regulatory structure. This decision was made in response to concerns raised by NDA allies TDP and NPP.
items.summary: The Centre has agreed to amend the Higher Education Bill, leaving State universities out of certain aspects of the regulatory structure. This decision was made in response to concerns raised by NDA allies TDP and NPP. The amendment will provide more autonomy to State universities and address the concerns of the States. The Higher Education Bill aims to promote quality education and improve the regulatory framework for higher education in India. The amendment will also ensure that the States have more control over their universities and can make decisions that are in the best interest of their students.
